references.context: Category theory: fibre category E_U of a functor p:E→C over U∈C; objects are x∈E with p(x)=U and morphisms are arrows α:x→y in E whose image under p is id_U.
references.reason: The fibre-category construction is independently useful beyond fibre categories that happen to be setoids; arbitrary base-changing arrows are not fibre-category arrows.
references.matching_note: Compare with provisional fibre-category candidate missing.2736dd8ef54a06c79e42; preserve p(α)=id_U.

references.disposition: The stated condition holds for every U in C; it is not equivalent to the total category being a setoid.

references.context: Category theory: automorphism group Aut_C(x) of an object x, consisting of all invertible endomorphisms x→x with composition and identity; in a groupoid all arrows are invertible. This is distinct from a field-automorphism group or a subgroup of vertical automorphisms unless context requires it.
references.reason: The general object automorphism group is a reusable categorical construction; setoidness demands that this group be trivial for every object.
references.matching_note: Do not link to the existing field-extension automorphism group or equate trivial automorphism groups with disconnectedness.
